title: Leaders Who Make Lightning-Quick Decisions
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article examines when fast decision-making is an asset rather than a liability. The author warns that leaders who always decide instantly shouldn't be trusted, since no one can process every option that quickly, but argues that a faster gear for accurate decisions is a skill worth developing. The key ingredients identified are a strong grounding in one's own values and beliefs, plus deep familiarity with the relevant details and competing arguments — both of which let the unconscious mind reach good conclusions quickly. The piece frames quick decision-making as most reliable when it's the product of prior preparation rather than a shortcut around it, and reserves major decisions for slower, more deliberate treatment.
points: Leaders who always decide instantly are not trustworthy, since fast judgment isn't universally reliable.
Speed becomes an asset only when paired with high-quality, well-grounded decisions.
Strong personal values give leaders a faster, more reliable basis for quick judgment calls.
Deep familiarity with a decision's details lets leaders separate what matters from what doesn't, faster.
Major decisions still deserve more deliberate time and attention despite the value of speed elsewhere.
quotes: Leaders who always make lightning-fast decisions are not to be trusted.
However, developing a faster gear for making accurate decisions with speed is a skill good leaders work on.
Leaders who know what they stand for have an easier time assessing competing goals and issues and making a good call.
The more expert the decision-maker is about the ideas and issues connected to any decision, the faster they can operate in distinguishing what is important and what isn’t.
In fact, leaders often reach better conclusions quickly than they do when they engage more deliberately.
Good leaders ignore the speed limits on the road to effective everyday choices.
